step_by_step_reasoning:
1. Identified core infrastructure components: ELB fronting Elastic Beanstalk for front-end web traffic, connected directly to RDS for querying.
2. Identified the serverless API layer: API Gateway invoking three distinct Lambda functions running PHP via custom runtimes/layers.
3. Identified the asynchronous document ingestion pipeline: Top Lambda fetches/generates PDF invoices, writes them to S3, triggering event notifications into SQS queue.
4. Identified background event handling: SQS triggers Middle and Bottom Lambdas for async data processing, caching state in ElastiCache and persisting structured data into RDS.

graph.name: Enoptea Serverless Backend Architecture
graph.notes: Enoptea processes energy consumption and billing data for thousands of sites using AWS Elastic Beanstalk for the front-end and a serverless PHP backend with AWS Lambda, SQS, S3, ElastiCache, and RDS.

nodes.name: ELB
nodes.notes: Entry point for front-end client requests.

nodes.name: BEANSTALK
nodes.notes: Elastic Beanstalk hosting web front-end application on EC2.

nodes.name: API GATEWAY
nodes.notes: API Gateway routing API requests to serverless Lambda microservices.

nodes.name: Lambda Top
nodes.notes: Lambda function fetching or scraping invoices from provider customer portals using custom PHP runtime.

nodes.name: Lambda Middle
nodes.notes: Lambda function processing invoice data, reading/writing temporary state in ElastiCache.

nodes.name: Lambda Bottom
nodes.notes: Lambda function performing asynchronous background calculations and database operations.

nodes.name: S3 Bucket
nodes.notes: S3 bucket storing downloaded invoice PDFs.

nodes.name: SQS
nodes.notes: SQS queue decoupling S3 event notifications and triggering processing Lambdas.

nodes.name: ELASTICACHE
nodes.notes: In-memory cache for temporary state storage.

nodes.name: RDS
nodes.notes: Relational database holding main application and consumption data.

edges.notes: ELB forwards client web traffic to Elastic Beanstalk.
Elastic Beanstalk reads and writes directly to RDS.
Elastic Beanstalk issues requests to API Gateway.
API Gateway invokes Top Lambda for fetching bills.
API Gateway invokes Middle Lambda for calculations.
API Gateway invokes Bottom Lambda for background jobs.
Top Lambda retrieves or generates PDF invoices.
PDF invoices are saved to S3 Bucket.
S3 upload triggers SQS message queue.
SQS triggers Middle Lambda to process uploaded invoices.
SQS triggers Bottom Lambda for asynchronous handling.
Middle Lambda caches temporary computational data in ElastiCache.
Middle Lambda stores processed metrics into RDS.
Bottom Lambda updates records in RDS.
